title: ChatGPT reportedly generating real signatures of New Yorker artists and adding them to AI images
key_facts: Viral outputs shared on social media seem to show ChatGPT repeatedly adding fake signatures of prominent New Yorker staff cartoonists to its AI-generated images, as reported by Nieman Lab.
ChatGPT generated signatures of more than a dozen professional cartoonists; the artists were not asked permission or paid.
Cartoonist and contributor Emily Flake told Nieman Lab she could see 'the DNA of my work' in the image but it did not look like something she drew.
Mashable says the signatures are likely the result of the popularity of New Yorker cartoons online and internet-wide scraping for training data.

A New Yorker spokesperson said a 2024 Condé Nast-OpenAI deal did not grant permission to train on cartoons or use the logo and art in image generation, and that contributing cartoonists keep their copyright.
An OpenAI spokesperson said the company appreciates the community 'flagging bugs and unintended behavior' so it can address them.
ChatGPT now warns that such a prompt 'may violate our guardrails concerning similarity to third-party content' but still generates the images, signatures included.
quote_evidence: ChatGPT was able to generate the signatures of more than a dozen professional cartoonist and affix them to the fake images, often rendered in the signature style of the publication, Nieman Lab reported.
The artists were not asked permission or provided compensation.
However, ChatGPT will still generate images in the style, including signatures, the publication reported.
why_it_matters_hint: A chatbot is producing fake work that carries real artists' names, a fresh flashpoint in the dispute over AI training on creators' work.
event_date: First reported by Nieman Lab on 5 Oct 2026; Mashable pickup 12 Oct 2026
notes: Nieman Lab's own page (https://www.niemanlab.org/2026/10/chatgpt-is-adding-real-cartoonists-signatures-to-fake-new-yorker-cartoons/) returned 403, so the text was read on Mashable, which cites it. Other outlets (Futurism, TechSpot, Digital Trends, Daily Cartoonist, GIGAZINE) covered the story from 6 to 8 Oct 2026. Older news re-dated: the story is a week old by 12 Oct 2026.
